legend: Low-power photomicrograph showing tumour involving the thyroid in a multinodular pattern.
Vascular invasion is frequently present. Frequently, large vessels are involved.
Mushrooming capsular invasion with a predominantly macrofollicular architecture. This tumour was found to harbour a somatic DICER1 mutation.
CD31 immunohistochemistry highlights endothelial cells in this focus of vascular invasion.
The tumours have a follicular architecture and are composed of cells with round normochromatic nuclei.

FNA specimen diagnosed as suspicious for a follicular neoplasm. Note the microfollicular architecture, round nuclei, and coarse chromatin. The cytological findings are not diagnostic of malignancy, because malignancy is based on the assessment of invasion in the resection specimen. The resection specimen was a minimally invasive follicular thyroid carcinoma.

Schematic drawing for the interpretation of the presence or absence of capsular invasion. The diagram depicts a follicular neoplasm (red) surrounded by a fibrous capsule (green). A Bosselation on the inner aspect of the capsule does not represent capsular invasion. B Sharp tumour bud invades into but not through the capsule, suggesting invasion and requiring deeper sections to exclude. C Tumour totally transgresses the capsule invading beyond the outer contour of the capsule, qualifying as capsular invasion. D Tumour clothed by thin (probably new) fibrous capsule but already extending beyond an imaginary (dotted) line drawn through the outer contour of the capsule, qualifying as capsular invasion. E A satellite tumour nodule with similar cytoarchitecture to that of the main tumour lying outside the capsule, qualifying as capsular invasion. If there is a background of adenomatous nodules, level sections should be considered to confirm that the focus is contiguous with the main mass. F Follicles aligned perpendicularly to the capsule, suggesting invasion and requiring deeper sections to exclude. G Follicles aligned parallel to the capsule do not represent capsular invasion. H Mushroom-shaped tumour with total transgression of the capsule qualifies as capsular invasion. I Mushroom-shaped tumour within but not through the capsule suggests invasion, requiring deeper sections to exclude. J Neoplastic follicles in the fibrous capsule with a degenerated appearance accompanied by lymphocytes and siderophages do not represent capsular invasion but rather capsular rupture related to prior FNA.
